findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/uri_review_R1/test_probe_w2.py: launcher '"%~dp0cmd.exe" /c "%~dp0real.bat" %*' gives realpath real.bat, interpreter cmd.exe, no error/unlaunchable. Any non-.exe/.com quoted file, including .bat/.cmd, counts as the 'script', and '%*' is accepted anywhere in the text (e.g. in a REM line). The reviewer then runs through cmd.exe, without /c, so stdin (the prompt) could be read as commands. This contradicts the plan's 'never through cmd.exe'. It needs a launcher already trusted at PLAN.
findings.suggested_fix: Owner criterion: a .cmd launcher that names cmd.exe (or powershell/pwsh) and a .bat/.cmd/.ps1 must not be bound or launched; %* must be on the launch line itself (not anywhere in the text, e.g. a REM line). Reviewer suggestion: Refuse a bound program whose basename is cmd.exe/powershell.exe/pwsh.exe, and refuse scripts with .bat/.cmd/.ps1 extensions; require %* on the line that names the program.
findings.title: A .cmd launcher naming cmd.exe and a .bat is bound and launched as [cmd.exe, x.bat] (DEV-LIFECYCLE-2-r2 R1-02, LOW, routed to repair by owner decision)

findings.evidence: _run catches OSError from proc.communicate() (after containment.spawn succeeded and the process was resumed) and returns status FAILED without containment.finish(proc). On Windows the job is neither terminated, nor appended to _OPEN_JOBS, nor recorded in _TAINTED, and the handle stays open, so KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE does not fire. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R2/probe/test_probe_unfinished.py with the repo's FakeApi/FakeProc: communicate raises OSError(23): job 1 = {'active': 1, 'terminated': False}, _OPEN_JOBS=[], _TAINTED=[], next C.precheck() = {'contained': True, 'killed': 0}. On Linux the leftover worker is a direct child in another session and the next sweep_orphans kills it, so only Windows is affected. Low likelihood: CPython swallows BrokenPipeError/EINVAL on the stdin write.
findings.suggested_fix: Coordinator-recommended, owner-approved: same fail-open class as R1-01 (fixed in 0ee6885a); every path after a successful spawn must end in containment.finish or leave the job tracked/tainted so the next precheck() fails closed. Fake-kernel32 regression test required. Reviewer suggestion: Register each job in _OPEN_JOBS at spawn time (remove it only once precheck/finish verified it empty), or call containment.finish(proc) in a finally on every path after a successful spawn (also run_cmd on non-TimeoutExpired exceptions).
findings.title: Windows: a worker whose communicate() raises OSError after spawn is never finished; its job stays unterminated and untracked, and the next precheck() reports contained=True (DEV-LIFECYCLE-2-r2 R2-01, LOW, routed to repair by owner decision)
